How to reduce your Cloudflare Workers, KV and R2 bill: levers ranked by dollar impact

A Workers Paid invoice is a monthly minimum plus separately metered usage: Worker requests, CPU time, KV reads and writes, and R2 storage and operations. R2 egress is free, so the money moves to operation counts. The useful question is not "how do I spend less" but "which line, changed by how much, saves the most". That is arithmetic you can do before the invoice, from the numbers in your dashboard.

1. Cache at the edge so the Worker never runs

Every request that reaches a Worker is billed as a request and as CPU time. Responses that rarely change can be served from the Cache API or the CDN cache instead. Serving 40% of 110M requests from cache removes 44M requests and the CPU time they used.

2. Skip redundant KV writes

KV writes cost ten times a read. Writing a value that has not changed, or updating a key on every request, is the fastest way to a surprising line. Compare before you write and batch updates. Of the 11M writes in the worked example, 40% fewer saves about $22 a month, more than any Workers-side change.

3. Cache hot KV keys

A small set of keys usually takes most reads. Hold them in the Worker's memory for the life of the isolate or in the Cache API. Halving 60M reads saves about $15.

4. Put the CDN in front of hot R2 objects

R2 reads are Class B operations. Serving a popular asset through the CDN cache means R2 is only asked on a miss; 60% fewer reads on 110M is about $24.

5. Batch R2 writes

Class A operations (writes, lists) cost more than twelve times a read. Use larger multipart parts, avoid listing a bucket on every request and write fewer, larger objects.

6. Trim CPU time and expire old objects

CPU time is cheap per millisecond but scales with traffic: lazy-parse large JSON, shrink the bundle and keep heavy work off the hot path. For storage, lifecycle rules that expire old objects and abort stale multipart uploads keep the GB-months from only growing.

Run it on your numbers

Enter your usage in the estimator or from the CLI, and gate a budget in CI:

node cli.mjs estimate usage.csv --budget 100

What this cannot see

Plans, add-ons, contracts and price changes are outside it. Prices here are approximate list prices and editable. The estimate is arithmetic on your inputs, never a bill reader.

Common questions

Which Cloudflare costs usually dominate?

It depends on the workload. Request-heavy APIs are dominated by Worker requests and CPU time; apps that write to KV on every request are dominated by KV writes; media and backup workloads by R2 operations. Estimate your own mix with the estimator rather than assuming.

Is there a minimum on Workers Paid?

Workers Paid carries a monthly minimum, so the bill never falls below it however little you use. The estimator shows the minimum as a floor and lets you edit it.

Do the savings add up?

No. Edge caching and CPU trimming act on the same Worker CPU time, so each lever is calculated alone and the list is a ranking, not a plan total.

CLOUDFLARE BILL ESTIMATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What will your Cloudflare bill be, and what cuts it most?

Enter your usage from the Cloudflare dashboard and get an estimated monthly bill by line and a ranked list of levers (edge caching, CPU trimming, KV caching, redundant KV writes, R2 lifecycle, R2 batching, CDN in front of R2) with a dollar saving for each.

Nothing is uploaded. Calculated in this browser from numbers you enter and approximate list prices you can edit. It cannot see your plan or your invoice.

1. Your monthly usage

2. Estimate

LineBillablePer month

Levers that cut the bill most

ChangeAssumptionSaves per month

Each lever is computed alone under the assumption shown. Levers overlap, so the savings are not additive.

Prices, allowances and assumptions (editable)

LinePrice per unit (USD)Included per month

Change a price here and press Estimate. Defaults are approximate list prices; check Cloudflare pricing and your plan.

Prefer a CLI, or want a budget gate in CI?

node cli.mjs template > usage.csv
node cli.mjs estimate usage.csv
node cli.mjs estimate usage.csv --budget 100      # exit 1 over budget
node cli.mjs estimate usage.csv --set r2_storage_gb=200 --json
node cli.mjs estimate usage.csv --prices prices.json --assume assumptions.json

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: how to reduce your Cloudflare bill.

Common questions

Does this read my Cloudflare account or invoice?

No. It reads only the usage numbers you type or paste (copy them from the Billing and the Workers and R2 analytics pages of the Cloudflare dashboard) and multiplies them by list prices you can edit. It cannot see your plan, add-ons, contract or real invoice. Treat every figure as a way to compare options, never as what you will be charged.

Where do the prices come from?

They are approximate public usage-based list prices from Cloudflare's Workers, KV and R2 pricing pages as best known in 2025, shown with an as-of date, and every one is editable, including the included allowances and the monthly minimum. Cloudflare changes prices and packaging, so check developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing before relying on a number.

How is the saving for each lever calculated?

Each lever re-runs the estimate with one change applied under an assumption shown beside it (for example, edge caching that serves 40% of requests without running the Worker) and reports the difference. The assumptions are editable. Levers overlap, so the savings are not additive.

Is my usage data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page calculates in your own browser and never sends anything. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.
